subject: storytime
title: The Princess and the Pea
about: Hans Christian Andersen's 1835 tale of the soaking-wet girl who says she is a real princess, and the queen who tests her with one little pea under twenty mattresses. It is short, silly and easy to picture, with a funny ending, and a good story for talking about where and when a story happens. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Ask: could you feel one little pea under twenty mattresses, and why did the queen think only a real princess could?

book.author: Hans Christian Andersen (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Twenty mattresses, one little pea, and one very real princess.

passage.text:
Once upon a time, there was a prince.
He lived in a castle with his mother, the queen.
He wanted to marry a real princess.
He looked all around the land.
He met lots of princesses.
But he could not tell if they were real.
So he went back home, feeling sad.
***
One night, there was a big storm.
The rain came down and the wind blew.
Knock, knock, knock!
A girl stood at the castle door.
She was very wet.
Water dripped from her hair.
Water ran out of her shoes!
"I am a real princess," she said.
"We will see about that," said the queen.
***
The queen went to get a bed ready.
She put one little green pea on the bed.
She did not tell the girl.
On top of the pea, she put a mattress.
Then another, and another, and another!
Soon there were twenty mattresses.
The bed was so tall!
The girl climbed a ladder to the top.
"Good night!" said the queen.
***
In the morning, the queen asked, "How did you sleep?"
"Oh, very badly!" said the girl.
"Something hard was in my bed."
"I tossed and turned all night."
"Now I am sore all over!"
The queen smiled a big smile.
Only a real princess could feel one little pea!
***
The prince was so happy.
He had found a real princess at last!
Soon they got married.
And the little green pea?
It went in a glass box for all to see.
After that, the princess slept on just one mattress.

cards.q: Who knocked at the castle door?
cards.note: Water ran out of her shoes, but she said she was a real princess.

cards.q: Where did the queen hide the pea?
cards.note: One little pea at the bottom, then twenty mattresses piled on top of it.

cards.q: What did the girl climb to get to the top?
cards.note: Twenty mattresses make a bed so tall you need a ladder to get in.

cards.q: How did the queen know she was a real princess?
cards.note: Only a real princess, the queen thought, could feel one little pea through all those mattresses.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The prince looked all around the land for a real princess before the stormy night.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: And the pea went in a glass box for all to see.

cards.q: How did the girl feel in the morning?
cards.note: She tossed and turned all night; ask him how one little pea could feel so big.

cards.q: When did the girl come to the castle?
cards.note: The setting is when and where a story happens: a castle, on a stormy night.

cards.q: In the story, what is a 'mattress'?
cards.note: A mattress is the thick, soft part of a bed that you sleep on.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
